solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mo changes exotic tight-fitting dress

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Mo swaps into an exotic, close-fitting outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like it describes the dress, but it signals rearranging the nine letters of MO CHANGES.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheongsam is a high-collared, close-fitting Chinese gown, a qipao.

clue.text: Caught a pair heading for Italian island

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: heading for takes the front letter of the word Italian

explanation.surface: A couple caught setting off for an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' seems to describe the island but only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: I resolved to reform bad people

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of I resolved are rearranged

explanation.surface: A New Year resolution to turn wrongdoers into better people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' is part of the letters, not a verb: 'to reform' rearranges I RESOLVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers or villains are people who commit wicked acts.

clue.text: Identifies those responsible as men, perverted celebrities

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so the letters of as men are rearranged

parts.note: famous people are big names

explanation.surface: A scandal exposing celebrities as perverts.
explanation.definitionFit: To name names is to identify culprits publicly, an idiom for informing.

clue.text: Height of bust about right

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the sculpture goes round the letter

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture, a kind of statue

explanation.surface: How tall a sculpted bust stands, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' is a sculpture, not a chest measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means a person's natural height.

clue.text: Curse male with girl

parts.note: Alison is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Swearing at a man and a woman together.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a malediction, the opposite of benison.

clue.text: With flaw in one piece

parts.note: a hole in an argument is a flaw or weakness

explanation.surface: Something flawed yet somehow still intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken and complete is entire, intact.

clue.text: Insect in meadow, as portrayed

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A bug pictured in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a stinging winged insect.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant pending

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Nothing pleasant is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan kept on ice is deferred, waiting: an idiom for postponed.

clue.text: Discerning journalist pocketing the old former US gold coin first

indicators.note: first puts the coin at the front of the answer

parts.note: the eagle was a ten-dollar US gold coin

indicators.note: pocketing means taking into a pocket, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed reporter pockets an antique American gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The eagle was a US ten-dollar gold coin, no longer minted; 'first' tells you it leads, ahead of the journalist and his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-sighted and observant, missing no detail.

clue.text: Stiffly formal welcoming a king of Troy

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal

explanation.surface: A starchy figure greeting a Trojan monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the ruler of Troy during the Trojan War, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Odd abiding issue involving novelist, an apparent misfortune that turned out well in the end

definitions.text: an apparent misfortune that turned out well in the end

indicators.note: involving means including or wrapping round, so the novelist goes inside the rearranged letters
odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of abiding issue are rearranged

parts.note: Doris Lessing was a Nobel-winning British novelist

explanation.surface: A strange, lingering problem with an author turns out to be good luck after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges only the twelve letters of 'abiding issue'; the novelist Doris Lessing is kept intact and sits near the front of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a setback that later proves beneficial, a hidden benefit.

clue.text: See 10
First of editorials in this newspaper on opening of Edinburgh festival

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the newspaper's abbreviation

parts.note: the clue appears in the Financial Times, abbreviated FT

indicators.note: first of picks out the initial letter of the word editorials
opening of takes the first letter of the word Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Editorials in the FT preview the start of the Edinburgh festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this newspaper' is the FT, where the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a public celebration or fair, a festival.

clue.text: Typical when reading to secure entrance to university

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: perusal is a careful reading

indicators.note: entrance to takes the opening letter of the word university

explanation.surface: Studying hard to get into university, the usual story.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the normal way, as is customary.

clue.text: Quietly tell ecclesiastical dignitary

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: Whispering something to a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other high-ranking cleric.

clue.text: Border: safe crossing eastern edge

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the safe stretches round the other pieces

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A safe crossing point on a country's eastern frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is underworld slang for a safe; a safecracker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the boundary line enclosing an area.

clue.text: Bouquet one's arranged — brilliant

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of one's are rearranged

parts.note: gay in its older sense means bright and brilliant

explanation.surface: Someone admires a bouquet they arranged themselves as brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' fits a bouquet but rearranges ONE'S into NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant flowers, a posy.

clue.text: Safety barrier may cause warder to scoff

parts.note: a prison warder is a guard
to rail is to jeer or protest bitterly, to scoff

explanation.surface: A barrier that makes a prison officer sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective rail along a road edge or staircase.

clue.text: Have a high opinion of some in wire spectacles

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Admiring certain people who wear wire-rimmed glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in regard, a verb of admiration.

clue.text: Time to walk like a duck? Nonsense

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with a swaying duck-like gait

explanation.surface: Is it time to strut about like a duck? What rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle means silly, trivial talk, rubbish.

clue.text: Horse that is in lead has new lad on

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of lad

explanation.surface: A horse in the lead now has a new stable lad riding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like first place in a race, but it is the metal, given by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with irregular black and white patches.

clue.text: American writer on Hardy heroine and Emily Dickinson, say

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: An American writer comments on Tess and on Emily Dickinson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emily Dickinson' seems another subject but is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was an American female poet, an example of the word.

clue.text: Foremost of motels with superb staff

indicators.note: foremost of picks out the leading letter of the word motels

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent or superb

explanation.surface: The best motels boast superb employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' means employees in the surface but a ceremonial rod in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff of office, as carried before a mayor.

clue.text: Honest about film director

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Being candid about a film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the sense of free of wrongdoing, above board.

clue.text: What's needed to play Poohsticks, past events put aside?

definitions.meaning: Poohsticks, from Winnie-the-Pooh, is played by dropping sticks into a stream from a bridge and watching them float beneath it
an idiom for past troubles that are over and forgotten

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a flowing stream beneath a crossing; figuratively old grievances that no longer matter.

clue.text: Judge director admired

parts.note: to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A judge who admired a director.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is informally to think highly of them, so highly regarded.

clue.text: Let out without charge

definitions.meaning: to release a captive, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for releasing and an adjective for gratis.

clue.text: See 22
Not suitable, a Parisian apartment

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Paris flat that just will not do.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means inappropriate or unfitting, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Get up around noon for a light wash

indicators.note: around here means the first piece is placed round the second

parts.note: to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: Rolling out of bed at midday for a quick wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a quick wash in clean water, or a light hair tint.

clue.text: Weak-willed? See daily, drunk having imbibed litres

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in as a drink, so the letter goes inside
drunk means befuddled, so the letters of see daily are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who gets drunk daily and has downed litres is clearly weak-willed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges SEE DAILY into EASILY ED, and 'having imbibed' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person readily persuaded or influenced lacks willpower.
